newsitem.title: ERITREA: Asmara Brewery seen threatened by Ethiopian taxes.
newsitem.headline: Asmara Brewery seen threatened by Ethiopian taxes.

text.p: Eritrea's Asmara Brewery has reported progress in its expansion programme but new taxes imposed by Ethiopia means its export market is now threatened.

Asmara Brewery Acting Manager Stifanos Habtemariam said Ethiopia imposed a 150 percent excise tax and a 12 percent sales tax since January on beer imports. There is also a 75 percent excise tax and a 12 percent sales tax on imported liquor.
In addition to this, the brewery pays a 100 percent excise tax and a 12 percent sales tax to the Eritrean government.
Stifanos said that up to January, Eritrea and Ethiopia had a bilateral trade agreement allowing both countries to export and import without being taxed in either country.
But Ethiopia ended the agreement at the start of the year.
Stifanos said Eritrea was not imposing any excise tax on Ethiopian goods (beer and liquor) being imported by Eritrea.
He said that before January, 15 percent of the brewery's beer production and 20 percent of its liquor production was sold in Ethiopia. But that has since been reduced to zero.
The name Asmara Brewery was conjured up in 1983 for a former Italian family concern called Melotti Brewery from 1939.
It produces lager beer, gin, cognac and fernet branca. The 6,000 bottles of hard liquor and 200,000 bottles of beer put out every day are currently all consumed in Eritrea.
"We used to sell beer to northern Ethiopia and liquor to all parts of Ethiopia, but since January Ethiopia put tax on all beer import," Stifanos told Reuters.
Asmara Brewery was on the September 1996 list of companies which the government said it intended to sell and has carried out a major expansion programme in the last year.

In March, the government asked for bids for the first nine companies on the privatisation list of 39 companies. Asmara Brewery was not included and privatisation officials would not say whether it would be in the next batch in May.
"We have now completed the first phase of expansion, with machinery worth more than $5 million. The first phase included the brew house and the fermentation section," Stifanos said.
"The second phase will be bottling. A new bottling line will be installed with a capacity of 60,000 bottles per hour.

"The estimated cost is 30 million birr and we have got approval from the government to go ahead with the new bottling line project study," he said, adding that there had so far been no financial input for the project from government.
Asmara Brewery reported a gross profit of 30 million birr for 1996 and turnover was more than 150 million birr.
"After the expansion, we have an expectation to export to other countries. We have a demand from Germany and Italy, but we would export mainly to surrounding countries," said Stifanos.
"In 1996 we produced 250,000 hectolitres (2.5 million litres) of beer. With full expansion, we will produce at least 400,000 hectolitres (4.0 million litres)," Stifanos added.
